title: Anthropic's Mythos Pass
seo_title: Anthropic Splits Claude Into Fable and Mythos
excerpt: On November 9 Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 as the same underlying model with different doors. Fable ships to everyone with classifiers that block high-risk cyber and biology work, then falls back to older Opus models when those classifiers fire. Mythos keeps the same weights with more permissive safeguards, and Anthropic hands that door only to organizations that clear its Cyber or Life Sciences Verification Programs. The upgrade story is speed and price. The governance story is a private passport for dual-use capability.
hero_alt: A row of natural-wood colored pencils with multicolored tips standing on a white surface
paragraphs: Anthropic did not ship one new frontier model on November 9. It shipped one set of weights under two product names, [Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2), and made the naming do the ethics work.
Fable is the public door. Mythos is the pass.

## Same weights, different permissions

Anthropic's own line is blunt: Fable and Mythos are the same underlying model. Fable carries strong cybersecurity and biology safeguards so the company can sell it widely. Organizations that want the dual-use work Anthropic is afraid to leave open apply through the [Cyber Verification Program](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604842-cyber-verification-program) or the Life Sciences track and, if approved, get Mythos.

That is not a second training run. It is a second permission state. The capability lives in both names. The difference is who Anthropic will let ask the dangerous questions without a classifier slamming the gate.

On Fable, high-risk cyber prompts can fall back to Claude Opus 4.8. Biology blocks fall back to Opus 5. Anthropic says early testing across claude.ai, Claude Code, and Cowork saw about 55 percent fewer unnecessary blocks than Fable 5.1, including roughly 60 percent fewer in cybersecurity and 40 percent fewer in biology. Fewer false positives is a product win. It does not dissolve the architecture. The public model still routes the sharpest dual-use work away from the new weights.

## What the pass buys

Mythos is where Anthropic wants the cyber and life-sciences scores to live. On the company's CVE Rediscovery eval, Mythos 5.2 found more published vulnerabilities from pre-fix snapshots than Mythos 5.1 or Opus 5.5. Anthropic also cites higher CyScenarioBench and protein-design numbers for Mythos, then reminds readers that Fable's safeguards will block most of that cybersecurity work.

Claude Enterprise customers get a partial compromise: Claude Security can run on Mythos 5.2 without every seat joining the Cyber Verification Program. The rest of the market meets Fable, the fallbacks, and an application portal.

Pricing is identical for both names: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, with an optional fast mode at double those rates. The bill does not tell you which moral regime you bought. The model id does.

## A private licensing state

Labs already decide what a chat interface will refuse. Anthropic's move is sharper because the refusal is productized as a twin SKU. Fable is the export-controlled version of the company's own mind. Mythos is the licensed one.

That structure has real virtues. Independent researchers and bug-bounty hunters can apply for Defense Access without pretending every Claude user needs binary exploit help. Hospitals and cyber firms can argue for reduced classifiers without Anthropic shipping those classifiers off by default. Distillation defenses got stronger too; Anthropic claims the new techniques cut harvested training data from illicit distillers by 90 to 99 percent.

The cost sits elsewhere. A private company now runs a visa desk for frontier dual-use skill. Who counts as "beneficial" cybersecurity or biomedical research is an Anthropic judgment call, reviewed through Anthropic portals, under Anthropic usage policies that still ban mass destruction, denial-of-service, and stated malicious intent even for verified tiers. Governments regulate export licenses in public statutes. Anthropic regulates Mythos in help-center prose.

Sonar already tracked how [Anthropic wants to sell stock without selling the steering wheel](/article/who-controls-anthropic-after-it-sells-stock). The Mythos pass is the same instinct at the API layer: keep the dangerous verbs inside a narrower circle, then call the circle safety.

## The judgment

Fable 5.2 is a serious technical release. Faster output, lower price, and a long list of demos from operating-system builds to formalized math will dominate the launch posts. The lasting design choice is the pass.

Anthropic is admitting, in product form, that the useful model for cyber and biology is also the misuse model. Anthropic declined a single public answer. It built a lobby. That may be the least bad private option available in 2026. It is still a private option. The public gets Fable, the fallbacks, and a wait for someone else's approval stamp. Mythos holders get the same mind with fewer tripwires. Same weights. Different citizenship.
